Area.evidence_source: [page/5/Text/9] The theme is understood as longing for being understood and loved (9–12), which can account for a risk of suicide (30). [page/5/Text/10] Extensive research has shown that hopelessness is the link between depression and increased risk of suicide (34). [page/5/Text/10] Longings and desires are about the future and bring hope for something or someone who can help. Hope is understood as relational (33). [page/5/Text/11] According to Lindstrom, allowing oneself to be touched by the other's longing might be a gateway to breaking through the 'shimmer of loneliness' (10) and to relieving life suffering (16, 17). [page/5/Text/12] Mental illness is considered a major factor in most suicides and suicide attempts (1, 3, 36). [page/5/Text/13] Isolation provides more space and 'nutrition' for suicidal thoughts, and in the data, it is compared to 'a seed that grows and overshadows everything'. [page/6/Text/2] In this struggle, this study showed a reflection about moral responsibility towards himself and especially towards related persons, as also reported by Tzeng (14). [page/6/Text/3] Suicidality functions as a survival strategy, and as a way of problem solving (41), until what was experienced as comforting becomes a threat, and suicide then appears to be the solution. [page/6/Text/4] In this study, shame and guilt are associated with failure because the persons neither cope with own life nor are they being successful with the suicidal attempt. [page/6/Text/5] On the other hand, a respectful attitude from professional helpers contributes to reduce shame (12– 14, 46).
